betaine.summary: Beet-derived training supplement lifters take for strength, power and a fuller, leaner look.

quick.overview:
Betaine (trimethylglycine) is a compound found in beets, spinach, wheat and shellfish, and sold as a pre-workout supplement. Lifters take it for more strength and power and a fuller, better-hydrated muscle look.

It acts as an osmolyte that protects cells under stress and as a methyl donor, and proponents link it to cell hydration, creatine synthesis and anabolic signalling. A meta-analysis found a small gain in maximal strength, mainly lower body, while results for body composition and power are mixed across small, short trials.
quick.how: Taken as a powder or capsule, often inside pre-workout blends, on training days or daily alongside other staples such as creatine. Trials have run for a few weeks, and users judge it by how heavy and how many reps they can handle over a training block.
quick.risks: Legal and low in acute toxicity. Stomach upset and a fishy odor can occur, and it may raise cholesterol in some people. A prescription form exists for homocystinuria, and betaine hydrochloride sold for digestion is a different product.

angle.text: Users take betaine as a training supplement to get more strength and power, which feeds harder, heavier sessions and a fuller, leaner muscle look. Small trials have measured strength and body composition with mixed results. Claims about cortisol and overtraining come mostly from limited or anecdotal reports.

ashwagandha.summary: Ayurvedic adaptogen taken to cut stress and improve sleep and recovery so you train harder and build more muscle.

quick.overview:
Ashwagandha is a shrub whose root is a staple of Ayurvedic medicine, sold as an extract for stress, sleep and vitality. In fitness it is taken for better recovery, strength and testosterone support, with a more muscular, less stressed look as the goal.

Its withanolides appear to calm the stress axis, lower cortisol and affect GABA and inflammatory signalling, so any muscle effect comes through better stress, sleep and recovery rather than direct anabolism. Small randomized trials report modest gains in strength and some hormone readings, and meta-analyses report lower stress and anxiety scores. Visible appearance changes have not been studied directly.
quick.how: Taken daily as a root powder or standardized extract capsule, often in the evening, and stacked with sleep and recovery supplements. Trials run for weeks to a couple of months, and users usually notice stress and sleep changes before any training effect.
quick.risks: Sold as a supplement in most countries. Rare cases of liver injury have been reported, and it can affect thyroid hormone levels and cause drowsiness or stomach upset. It is generally avoided in pregnancy and may interact with thyroid, sedative and immunosuppressant drugs.

angle.text: Ashwagandha is taken to lower stress, improve sleep and nudge testosterone, so you recover faster, train harder and build more muscle. Small human trials report modest changes in strength, stress scores and some hormone readings. Visible appearance changes have not been directly studied.

turkesterone.summary: Plant ecdysteroid marketed to bodybuilders as a natural anabolic for muscle gain without hormone suppression.

quick.overview:
Turkesterone is a plant steroid (a phytoecdysteroid) first isolated from Ajuga turkestanica and sold as a natural alternative to anabolic steroids. Bodybuilders take it hoping for muscle growth and a fuller physique without suppressing their own hormones.

In animals, ecdysteroids increased muscle protein synthesis, apparently through estrogen receptor beta and signalling pathways rather than the androgen receptor. Most support comes from rodent studies and work on the related ecdysterone. Human studies of turkesterone are small and short, including a 2024 acute study of 11 men that found no significant effect on IGF-1 or metabolic measures.
quick.how: Sold as capsules or powder, usually taken daily alongside a normal training and protein routine, sometimes with other ecdysteroid or muscle-building supplements. Users generally judge it over several weeks of training.
quick.risks: Sold as a dietary supplement in the US, with unresolved novel-food status in the EU. Short-term human studies have not reported serious harm, but long-term data are lacking. Independent testing has found products with far less turkesterone than labelled.

angle.text: Turkesterone is promoted to bodybuilders as a natural anabolic that builds muscle and a fuller physique without suppressing your own hormones. The idea comes from animal and cell studies of ecdysteroid signalling, plus sellers' marketing and user reports. Human trials of turkesterone itself are small.

ecdysterone.summary: Plant-derived ecdysteroid lifters take for muscle gain, with one human trial reporting larger gains alongside training.

quick.overview:
Ecdysterone (20-hydroxyecdysone) is the molting hormone of insects and crustaceans, also found in plants such as spinach and Cyanotis. Lifters take it as a plant-derived anabolic, with some promoting it as a hormone-neutral way to add muscle and a bigger physique.

In rodents it stimulates muscle protein synthesis without androgen receptor activity, with evidence pointing to estrogen receptor beta and Akt signalling. A 2019 controlled study funded by the World Anti-Doping Agency reported larger gains in muscle mass and bench press with ecdysterone alongside training, while a 2006 study found no significant effect on training adaptations. Replication is sparse.
quick.how: Sold as capsules or powder and taken daily alongside a normal training and protein routine over several weeks. It is also being developed as an investigational compound for muscle conditions.
quick.risks: Acute toxicity appears low. It is sold as a supplement, though the World Anti-Doping Agency has monitored it. Product purity is reported to vary, and long-term human safety has not been established.

angle.text: Lifters take ecdysterone as a plant-derived anabolic to add muscle on top of training, some describing it as hormone-neutral. One controlled human study reported larger gains in muscle mass and bench press with it, and cell and animal work points to estrogen receptor beta. Product quality is a recurring concern.

testosterone.summary: The main male hormone, behind muscle, bone and masculine features, used medically for deficiency and in physique culture.

quick.overview:
Testosterone is the principal male sex hormone, made mainly in the testes. It builds muscle and bone, drives body hair, voice deepening and the jaw and brow development of puberty, and it shapes the leaner, more masculine physique people associate with high levels.

It binds the androgen receptor, raising muscle protein synthesis, satellite cell activity and bone formation, and is partly converted to estradiol and DHT. It is prescribed as replacement therapy for diagnosed hypogonadism, where benefit is well documented. Healthy young men given supraphysiologic amounts gain muscle in a dose-dependent way, and anabolic steroid use is a staple of bodybuilding. Claims about changing facial structure in adults are mostly anecdotal.
quick.how: Medically it is delivered by injection, gel, patch or other forms under physician supervision, with blood monitoring, as replacement therapy. In physique circles it is discussed as TRT or as higher-level steroid use, usually combined with heavy training and diet. Muscle changes appear over weeks to months.
quick.risks: Prescription-only and a controlled substance in many countries. Documented risks include suppression of natural production and fertility, acne, polycythemia, blood pressure and lipid changes, mood effects and possible cardiovascular strain, and stopping abruptly can leave a deficiency. This entry is informational, not guidance for use.

angle.text: Testosterone is the hormone behind muscle, jaw and brow development, body hair and voice, and it is used as replacement therapy (TRT) or at high levels for physique. More androgen signalling means more muscle and bone mass and a leaner, more masculine build. Muscle effects are well studied in medical and trial settings; claims about enhancing adult facial structure are mostly anecdotal.

somatropin.summary: Prescription growth hormone used for body composition, with fuller, leaner physique effects and facial changes with chronic excess.

quick.overview:
Somatropin is recombinant human growth hormone, identical in sequence to the pituitary hormone. People use it for leaner, fuller physiques, fat loss and anti-ageing, and in bodybuilding circles for a so-called steroid look with a wider jaw and face.

It activates growth hormone receptors and the JAK2/STAT pathway, prompting the liver and other tissues to make IGF-1, which drives growth, fat mobilization and changes in fluid balance. In adults with diagnosed deficiency, replacement improves body composition and lipids. In healthy people, studies report some added lean mass with limited strength benefit. The facial claims are anecdotal, and chronic excess produces acromegaly.
quick.how: Medically it is prescribed for children and adults with growth hormone deficiency and some other conditions under specialist care. Outside medicine it is used in bodybuilding and physique communities, often alongside anabolic steroids, over months.
quick.risks: Prescription-only and banned in sport. Side effects include fluid retention, joint pain, carpal tunnel syndrome and insulin resistance. Chronic excess causes acromegaly, with enlargement of the jaw, brow and hands, plus heart and metabolic problems and a possible cancer link. This is informational, not guidance for use.

angle.text: Users take synthetic growth hormone for muscle, fat loss, anti-ageing and, in bodybuilding circles, a wider jaw and face. Raised GH and IGF-1 shift body composition toward more lean mass and less fat. It is approved for deficiency states, where its effects are studied; use in healthy adults for appearance is off-label and the facial claims are anecdotal.

mk-677.summary: Oral ghrelin mimic that raises growth hormone and IGF-1 for recovery, sleep and appetite to help bulking.

quick.overview:
MK-677 (ibutamoren) is an oral drug that mimics ghrelin and raises growth hormone and IGF-1. Users take it for better recovery and sleep and for the strong appetite boost that makes bulking easier, and some younger users hope it adds height.

It activates the ghrelin receptor in the pituitary and hypothalamus, producing pulsatile growth hormone release and higher IGF-1. Trials in older adults, obese men and dieting volunteers showed raised GH and IGF-1 and increased fat-free mass, without clear functional gains. No trial has tested it for cosmetic outcomes in healthy people.
quick.how: Taken as an oral research chemical, usually daily, by lifters during bulking phases and discussed as an oral alternative to injectable growth hormone. Users typically report appetite and sleep changes first, with body changes over weeks to months.
quick.risks: Never approved for any use, and prohibited in sport. Reported effects include increased appetite, fluid retention, lethargy and reduced insulin sensitivity, and a heart failure signal appeared in one trial. Long-term effects of sustained IGF-1 elevation are unknown, and products may be mislabelled.

angle.text: MK-677 is an oral ghrelin mimic taken to raise growth hormone for recovery, sleep and a bigger appetite, which makes bulking and adding muscle easier. Trials show raised GH and IGF-1 and some lean-mass change in other populations. No trial has tested it for aesthetic outcomes.

cjc-1295.summary: Injectable GHRH peptide users take to raise growth hormone for recovery, sleep, leanness and skin.

quick.overview:
CJC-1295 is a synthetic analogue of growth hormone releasing hormone. Users take it to raise growth hormone and IGF-1 for recovery, fat loss, skin and sleep, and some younger users hope it adds height.

It binds the GHRH receptor on the pituitary, increasing growth hormone secretion, and the long-acting version attaches to albumin so one dose lifts GH and IGF-1 for days. Early human studies in healthy adults showed prolonged GH and IGF-1 rises. No published trial has shown muscle, fat-loss or cosmetic changes in healthy people.
quick.how: Used as an injectable research peptide, often combined with the ghrelin mimic ipamorelin, and reported by forum users as prescribed by some clinics. Users usually describe sleep and recovery changes first, with body-composition goals over months.
quick.risks: Not an approved medicine, sold as a research peptide, and banned in sport. A phase II trial was halted after a participant died, though the physician thought it was likely unrelated to the drug. Reported effects include flushing, headache, water retention and injection-site reactions. Long-term safety is unknown and the status of compounded versions has been in flux.

angle.text: CJC-1295 is an injectable peptide taken to raise growth hormone and IGF-1, aiming at better recovery and sleep and a leaner, younger-looking physique. Human data come from a few endocrine studies showing raised GH and IGF-1. The appearance claims rest on user reports.

ipamorelin.summary: Selective GH-releasing peptide users take for recovery, sleep and hoped-for height, often alongside CJC-1295.

quick.overview:
Ipamorelin is a synthetic peptide that selectively triggers growth hormone release. Users, including some teenagers and young adults, take it hoping for added height, better sleep and recovery, and facial bone growth, usually alongside CJC-1295.

It activates the ghrelin receptor to produce pulsatile pituitary GH release, with little effect on cortisol and prolactin compared with older secretagogues. Human work is limited to early pharmacology and a post-surgical bowel recovery trial that showed no clear benefit. No published data show height, facial or muscle changes.
quick.how: Sold as a research peptide for injection, commonly stacked with a GHRH analogue such as CJC-1295, and used by some athletes and physique enthusiasts. Users typically report sleep and recovery changes before anything else.
quick.risks: Not approved for human use and banned in sport. Short-term data are limited; theoretical concerns include insulin resistance, fluid retention and the effects of long-term GH and IGF-1 elevation. Product quality is unregulated.

angle.text: Ipamorelin is a GH-releasing peptide taken, often by younger users alongside CJC-1295, for height while growth plates are open, better sleep and recovery, and facial bone growth. Human data are thin and focused on GH release. The height and facial claims rest on user reports.

sermorelin.summary: GHRH peptide that prompts your own growth hormone release, used off-label for recovery, leanness and anti-ageing.

quick.overview:
Sermorelin is a synthetic fragment of growth hormone releasing hormone, made of its first 29 amino acids. People use it hoping to raise growth hormone for leanness, sleep, recovery and anti-ageing, and some teenagers hope for added height.

It acts on GHRH receptors in the pituitary to prompt natural pulsatile GH release, so the body's feedback mechanisms still operate, unlike with injected GH. It was FDA-approved for diagnosing and treating growth hormone deficiency in children before manufacturing ceased in 2008. Reviews describe the hormonal mechanism as real, with limited controlled evidence of visible body-composition change in healthy adults.
quick.how: Available through compounding pharmacies and telehealth clinics, prescribed off-label as an injectable for age-related decline, body composition and recovery. Users typically report sleep and recovery changes over weeks and body changes over months.
quick.risks: Prescription-only in the US and banned in competitive sport. Common effects are injection-site reactions, flushing and headache. It is avoided with active cancer and in pregnancy. Compounded preparation quality and telehealth marketing claims are reported to vary.

angle.text: Sermorelin prompts your own pituitary to release more growth hormone, aiming at a leaner body, better sleep and recovery, and for some teenagers added height. It was approved in the past for diagnosing and treating GH deficiency in children. Use for cosmetic or height goals in healthy people is off-label and untested.

ghrp-6.summary: GH-releasing peptide that raises growth hormone and causes intense hunger, used by lifters for bulking and recovery.

quick.overview:
GHRP-6 is a synthetic hexapeptide that raises growth hormone and also triggers strong hunger. Users take it for muscle, recovery and fat loss, and many use the appetite surge to help them eat more while bulking.

It activates the ghrelin receptor, causing GH release and appetite stimulation, and also raises cortisol and prolactin somewhat. It has been used mainly as a research and diagnostic tool, including in tests for adult growth hormone deficiency. No published trial has shown improved muscle or appearance in healthy people.
quick.how: Sold as a research chemical for injection and used by bodybuilders mainly during bulking phases, where the hunger effect is the part users notice first, within the first hour of a dose.
quick.risks: Not approved for human use and banned in sport. Reported effects include intense hunger, water retention and flushing. Long-term safety is unknown and quality is unregulated.

angle.text: GHRP-6 is a GH-releasing peptide taken to raise growth hormone for muscle, recovery and fat loss, and for the strong hunger it causes, which some use to eat more while bulking. It has been studied in humans for GH release. Its effect on physique has not been tested.

igf-1-lr3.summary: Modified IGF-1 analogue sold to bodybuilders for muscle growth and repair.

quick.overview:
IGF-1 LR3 is a lab-modified version of insulin-like growth factor 1, sold to bodybuilders as an injectable for muscle growth and healing, sometimes stacked with insulin or steroids. The payoff people want is larger muscle, including targeted size where it is injected.

It activates the IGF-1 receptor and downstream PI3K/Akt/mTOR signalling. An extra amino acid chain and an arginine swap reduce binding to IGF binding proteins, so it is roughly three times as potent as native IGF-1 and lasts about 20 to 30 hours instead of 12 to 15. Evidence comes from cell and animal studies; no published human trial has tested it for muscle growth in healthy people.
quick.how: Sold as a research chemical for injection, used in bodybuilding circles alongside other agents. Forum discussion covers local-site growth and bloat, though these claims are not backed by trials.
quick.risks: Not approved for humans and banned in sport. Main concerns are low blood sugar, fluid retention, joint pain and organ growth, plus theoretical cancer promotion. Products are unregulated.

angle.text: IGF-1 LR3 is an injectable growth-factor analogue sold to bodybuilders for muscle growth and repair, sometimes stacked with insulin or steroids, aiming at larger muscle and local size. Cell and animal studies show IGF-1 signalling drives growth. Claims about local injection growth and bloat come from forums and vendors.

follistatin-344.summary: Injectable follistatin product sold to block myostatin and build muscle beyond natural limits.

quick.overview:
Follistatin-344 is the label for injectable follistatin preparations sold by peptide vendors to people who want more muscle than natural limits allow. Follistatin is a natural protein that binds and neutralizes myostatin, a protein that limits muscle growth.

In animals, blocking myostatin by gene knockout or raising follistatin levels produced larger muscles. Human work consists of gene-therapy studies, where a vector delivers the follistatin gene, rather than injections of a purified peptide. A 2026 narrative review of peptides marketed for performance included FS-344 among unapproved compounds and noted that results often come from animal models.
quick.how: Sold as a research peptide for injection and discussed on bodybuilding forums, mostly as speculation about effects. Some users pair it with training and diet or with food-based approaches, but these claims are anecdotal.
quick.risks: Not approved as a medicine in any major jurisdiction and banned in sport. Follistatin affects reproductive hormones and other tissues, so blocking these pathways raises theoretical concerns. Marketed peptides are unregulated and may not contain what is claimed.

angle.text: Follistatin-344 is an injectable sold to people hoping to block myostatin, lift the brake on muscle growth and build beyond natural limits. Follistatin has been studied in animals and in gene-therapy research. Vendor injectables are untested for this use in humans.

ostarine.summary: SARM lifters use for lean mass and a leaner look, trialled for muscle wasting.

quick.overview:
Ostarine (enobosarm, MK-2866) is an oral selective androgen receptor modulator used by lifters for lean mass and a leaner look, sometimes alongside TRT or after steroid cycles. It is regarded as a milder alternative to anabolic steroids.

It binds the androgen receptor aiming for activity in muscle and bone with less effect on tissues such as the prostate. Trials for muscle wasting, including lung cancer patients, showed increased lean mass without consistent functional gains. It was never approved, though development continues for other uses.
quick.how: Sold online as a research chemical or gym supplement and taken orally, typically for several weeks on a lean-bulk or cut, sometimes with post-cycle support. Users report gradual lean-mass and fullness changes.
quick.risks: Not approved and banned in sport. Reported harms include suppression of natural testosterone, lowered HDL cholesterol, raised liver enzymes and case reports of drug-induced liver injury. Gray-market products are often mislabelled.

angle.text: Ostarine is a SARM used by lifters to add lean mass and look leaner, sometimes alongside TRT or after steroid cycles. It activates the androgen receptor in muscle, which supports more muscle and some fat loss. It has been trialled for muscle wasting and raised lean mass there; hormone suppression is a documented effect.

lgd-4033.summary: SARM lifters use to add lean mass in a few weeks with less perceived hormonal impact than steroids.

quick.overview:
LGD-4033 (ligandrol) is an oral selective androgen receptor modulator that lifters take to add lean mass and a bigger, more muscular physique within weeks, with less perceived hormonal impact than steroids.

It activates the androgen receptor in muscle and bone and suppresses the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis. A randomised phase I trial in 76 healthy men found 21 days raised lean body mass, and a phase 2 trial after hip fracture reported dose-dependent lean-mass gains. In those trials, testosterone and HDL cholesterol fell.
quick.how: Sold online as a research chemical and taken orally for several weeks, often during bulks and sometimes with post-cycle support. Users report strength and fullness changes within the first weeks.
quick.risks: Not approved and banned in sport. Documented problems include testosterone suppression, reduced HDL cholesterol and drug-induced liver injury, especially at amounts above trial levels. Product contents are unreliable.

angle.text: LGD-4033 is a SARM used by lifters to add lean mass in a few weeks with less perceived hormonal impact than steroids. It activates the androgen receptor in muscle for a bigger, more muscular look. Small trials in older and young men showed lean-mass gains alongside hormonal suppression and lipid changes.

rad-140.summary: Potent SARM lifters use for muscle and fat loss, with liver and hormone effects reported.

quick.overview:
RAD-140 (testolone, vosilasarm) is an oral selective androgen receptor modulator that lifters use for muscle and fat loss, with some hoping for less suppression than steroids.

It binds the androgen receptor with tissue selectivity. Rat and monkey studies showed muscle-stimulating effects with weaker effects on the prostate. It is under development by Ellipses Pharma for androgen receptor-positive breast cancer, and the only completed human trial was a small first-in-human study in postmenopausal women with breast cancer. No human data on its effect on lean body mass have been published.
quick.how: Sold online as a research chemical and taken orally during bulks or cuts, often over several weeks. Users judge it by strength and leanness changes.
quick.risks: Not approved for physique use and banned in sport. Case reports describe drug-induced liver injury, myocarditis and heart failure in non-medical users, and it suppresses natural hormones. Many products sold as a specific SARM contain none of it or unrelated substances.

angle.text: RAD-140 is a potent SARM used by lifters for more muscle and less fat, with some hoping for less suppression than steroids. It activates the androgen receptor in muscle. It has been studied in animals and is in development for breast cancer; human data on physique are lacking, and liver and hormone effects are reported.

yk-11.summary: Steroid-like SARM marketed as a myostatin inhibitor for gains beyond ordinary SARMs.

quick.overview:
YK-11 is a steroid-based compound sold as a myostatin-inhibiting SARM, taken by users hoping for bigger gains than ordinary SARMs and a more muscular physique. It behaves as a partial agonist of the androgen receptor, and its classification is itself disputed.

In cultured muscle cells a 2013 study from Toho University reported increased follistatin expression and reduced myostatin signalling via androgen receptor activation. Published work consists of cell and animal studies, including sepsis-related muscle wasting; no human clinical trial has been found.
quick.how: Sold online as a research chemical, usually as an oral product, and discussed on bodybuilding forums as a step up from other SARMs. Users report effects based on training results over weeks.
quick.risks: Not authorised as a medicine and banned in sport. Safety is untested in humans, and liver, hormonal and cardiovascular effects are suspected. Health Canada has warned SARMs can pose risks such as heart attack, stroke and liver damage. Products are often mislabelled.

angle.text: YK-11 is a steroid-like compound sold as a myostatin-inhibiting SARM, which users take hoping for muscle gains beyond ordinary SARMs. In cultured muscle cells it raised follistatin and lowered myostatin signalling. Evidence is limited to cell and animal work, and its classification is disputed.

finasteride.summary: Approved oral DHT blocker that slows male pattern hair loss and helps keep your hairline and thickness.

quick.overview:
Finasteride is an oral drug that blocks the enzyme converting testosterone into DHT, the hormone that shrinks scalp follicles in male pattern hair loss. It is the most established medical treatment for keeping your hairline and thickness, and it is a core part of hair-loss routines, usually paired with minoxidil.

It lowers serum DHT by about 70 percent and scalp DHT by a similar amount, which reduces follicle miniaturisation and lets some follicles recover. In randomised trials and meta-analyses, the 1 mg hair-loss form outperformed placebo on hair counts and global assessments, with regrowth of about 15 percent reported in meta-analyses and the main effect being slowed loss. Benefit is lost within months of stopping.
quick.how: Taken as a daily tablet on prescription, long term, and paired with topical or oral minoxidil. Results are usually judged over six months to a year, and some men use lower-frequency or topical versions, which are debated.
quick.risks: Decreased libido, erectile dysfunction and ejaculatory problems occur in a minority, and depression, anxiety and suicidal thoughts have been reported. Some men describe persistent sexual or mood symptoms after stopping (post-finasteride syndrome), whose frequency and cause remain debated. It can affect PSA readings, is contraindicated in pregnancy, and women should not handle crushed tablets. It is prescription-only.

angle.text: Finasteride lowers DHT, which slows follicle miniaturisation and helps you keep or thicken scalp hair and hold your hairline. It is an approved drug with randomised trial data in men. Reported sexual and mood side effects, including persistent ones, are a major point of debate, as are lower-dose and topical regimens.

dutasteride.summary: Stronger DHT blocker than finasteride, used off-label to stop male pattern hair loss.

quick.overview:
Dutasteride blocks all three active 5-alpha-reductase enzymes, cutting circulating DHT by more than 90 percent compared with about 70 percent for finasteride. People use it as a stronger option to stop male pattern hair loss and hold or thicken scalp hair.

Because scalp follicles use the type I enzyme as well as type II, this broader blockade is thought to protect more follicles from DHT-driven miniaturisation. A phase III trial compared several amounts with finasteride and placebo, and a systematic review ranked dutasteride 0.5 mg above finasteride 1 mg for hair counts, though comparative trial data are limited. It is approved for hair loss in South Korea, Japan and Taiwan and used off-label elsewhere.
quick.how: Taken as a daily or periodic capsule on prescription, usually by people who respond poorly to finasteride or want stronger suppression, and often paired with minoxidil. Results are judged over six to twelve months, and topical or injected versions are discussed but less studied.
quick.risks: Reported effects resemble finasteride's, including reduced libido, erectile and ejaculatory problems, breast disorders and mood effects in some users. Its half-life of about 4 to 5 weeks means it stays in the body for months after stopping. It is contraindicated in pregnancy and affects PSA interpretation. It is prescription-only.

angle.text: Dutasteride blocks both 5-alpha-reductase types for stronger DHT suppression, slowing follicle miniaturisation so you keep or thicken scalp hair. It is used off-label in most countries and approved for hair loss in a few, with trial data there. Reported side effects and topical use are debated.

minoxidil.summary: Over-the-counter and low-dose oral treatment that regrows and thickens scalp hair, and is also used on beard and brows.

quick.overview:
Minoxidil regrows and thickens hair, giving a fuller scalp, and many people also apply it to the beard and brows. Topical forms (Rogaine and generics) are sold over the counter in many countries, and low-dose oral minoxidil is prescribed off-label.

It is converted to its active sulphate form in the follicle and is thought to prolong the growth phase, shorten the resting phase and enlarge shrunken follicles, possibly through blood flow and growth-factor signalling. It works independently of hormones, so it is often paired with finasteride or dutasteride. Meta-analyses found 2 percent and 5 percent topical forms superior to placebo in men, and a 2024 JAMA Dermatology trial compared oral and topical minoxidil. Beard and brow use is less studied.
quick.how: Applied as a solution or foam once or twice daily to the scalp, or taken as a low-dose oral tablet on prescription, long term. Early shedding in the first weeks is common, and visible results usually take several months.
quick.risks: Topical use can cause scalp irritation, dryness and unwanted facial hair, and propylene glycol can cause contact dermatitis. Oral use can cause excess hair growth, fluid retention, ankle swelling, fast heart rate and dizziness, and needs medical oversight. Gains are lost within months of stopping. It is toxic to cats if ingested.

angle.text: Minoxidil extends the hair growth phase and enlarges shrunken follicles, so scalp hair grows back thicker and denser, and many users apply it to the beard and brows too. Topical forms are approved for scalp hair loss; oral low-dose use is off-label with growing trial data. Beard and brow use is less studied.
